reachable: Yes, trivially and strongly. The coding changes the model's INPUT at every command position including the scored read, so every downstream parameter sees it and gets gradient through it; there are no new parameters to be dead. The head consumes it at full resolution — r2_dualaddress_move_transport reads tok[:, 0::2] (raw 768-d coded command tokens) through src_ext/dst_ext = nn.Linear(768, 256), so the SRC/DST block structure is available to a single linear map without passing through the trunk; the arch consumes it through cmd_proj + LayerNorm. Training reaches it: evolve/harness.py:83 calls stream.collate on the full sample dicts, realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:83 puts "cmds" on every sample, and _strip_target_only only removes exit_cls/z_delta, so cmds are always present and the coding never silently no-ops in training. Scoring reaches it: evolve/cups_probe.py:168-262 (stream_coded_toks) rebuilds the coding per arm from each arm's own command strings. Verified that collate's command tokens equal code_cmds(z_cmd) bitwise and that everything else (types, key_pad, tgt, cmd_mask, observation tokens, padding) is bit-identical to baseline_interleave. Head-side reachability at the read position is also intact: the transport read r_i and the injection gate depend only on the command token, and only the WRITE is gated by `active = valid_cmd & valid_obs`, which is the one condition ground truth says is false at the scored read — so the read still fires there.
solves_outside_model: No. This is the legitimate kind of command-string parsing. _parse splits one command string into verb/src/dst and _sparse_block hashes each PATH STRING with SHAKE-256 into a fixed coordinate block; nothing consults an earlier command, an observation, or any cross-step matching, and no content identity is ever computed. How I checked, by execution rather than reading: (1) position-wise purity — replacing every command except position i with "cat /zzz/other" leaves position i's coded token bit-identical, for all 8 positions; (2) prefix causality — code_cmds(cmds[:k], z[:k]) equals code_cmds(cmds, z)[:k] for every k; (3) the role-swap invariant, built directly — native ["mv /x/a /x/c","mv /x/b /x/d","cat /x/c"] vs swapped ["mv /x/b /x/c","mv /x/a /x/d","cat /x/c"] gives torch.equal on the read token and non-equal on the move tokens; (4) input z_cmd is cloned, never mutated, and the coding is deterministic across a cache clear (SHAKE-256, no Python hash()). This is the opposite shape from the retracted r2 stream: that one resolved the chain in Python and stamped the resolved content into the read token; this one only NAMES locations and, if anything, destroys lexical structure (hashing makes "sshd_config.cfg.6" and "sshd_config.cfg.2" unrelated), so the model must still integrate the moves to know which content sits at the read path. cups_probe's own read-token invariant (cups_probe.py:246-262) independently enforces this at score time.
summary: The code does what the "WHAT I ADDED" section says, and every safety-relevant claim is true under execution: layout untouched, observation tokens and tgt untouched, one command token = standardized z_cmd + a 63-coordinate sparse code drawn from that one command's own string, position-wise pure, prefix-causal, read token bit-identical under a role-swapped chain while the move tokens differ, deterministic, inputs not mutated, and collate 5.2x faster than baseline (16.7 ms -> 3.2 ms per call, matching the ~5x claim). The rigid-translate property is exact: the DST-block pattern of "mv A B" and the SRC-block pattern of "cat B" have cosine exactly 1.0. The routing is NOT computed outside the model. The one substantive miss is in the mechanistic justification, not the mechanism: the hypothesis says the two extractors "see byte-identical vectors for a given path", but the code is added on top of the sentence embedding on the same coordinates, so what src_ext and dst_ext actually see has cosine 0.165, with the shared component carrying only ~20% of the block energy. The cross-role composition is a learnable shared direction against a 4x-larger nuisance term, not free coordinate selection — the design's second pillar is real but weaker and less automatic than described. Two smaller overstatements: the "0.0" orthogonality figure is one lucky example (real off-diagonal max 0.25), and the energy cost is 25% rather than the estimated 17% (author flagged that one as unmeasured). Separately, a scoring caveat that is not a hypothesis mismatch: clean path symbols also make ONE-hop, non-tracking lookups cheaper, and the ground truth says move-order-keyed heuristics do not cancel on this frozen slice, so any gain must be read against the reported analytic band rather than against the parent's number alone. What I could NOT check: any claim requiring the real GPU lane — whether native_hit rises while swap_stayed holds, whether the r2 head's label-free mining actually fires on real observation embeddings (I have no local embedding cache; the premise that mv observations are identical is ground truth, but the dup_o/mut_between mining threshold behaviour on real z_obs is untested), and whether dropping the parent's r18 consistency head costs more than the transport head gains.

divergences.claim: "src_ext restricted to dims 0..351 and dst_ext restricted to dims 352..703 see byte-identical vectors for a given path, so the shared path_key composes correctly ... generically ... for paths never seen in training" (hypothesis lines 52-56).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code is ADDED to the standardized sentence embedding on the same coordinates, not written into free dimensions. The two block views therefore differ by two different slices of two different sentence embeddings. Measured on the real path "/tmp/w/cups/g53/f150.tmp" with unit-variance z_cmd: torch.equal(dst_view_of_mv, src_view_of_cat) is False, cos = 0.165, relative L2 difference 1.23. Only the CODE component is an exact rigid translate (cos = 1.000 exactly). The code carries 88 of ~444 units of block energy (~20%); under a generic random linear readout the path signal is 0.46x the amplitude of the embedding background. So the cross-role equality is a shared component the extractors must LEARN to isolate against a ~4x-larger nuisance term, not something "available by coordinate selection alone". The mechanism is real and new — no other impl supplies an exactly role-translated path component — but it is materially weaker and less automatic than the hypothesis states.
divergences.evidence: Executed: S.code_cmds(["mv A B","cat B"], torch.randn(2,768)); compared coded[0,352:704] vs coded[1,0:352] (cos 0.165, not equal) and (coded-z)[0,352:704] vs (coded-z)[1,0:352] (cos 1.000, exact). Head confirmed to read raw tokens: r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py:81-88,112,131-132 — src_ext/dst_ext are nn.Linear(768,h) applied to tok[:,0::2], path_key shared.

divergences.claim: "cos(DST block of the mv, SRC block of the cat) == 1.0 exactly, and 0.0 for 'cat B'' where B' differs from B by one trailing character" (lines 24-26).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The 1.0 half is exactly right (verified, exactly 1.0). The 0.0 half is an unrepresentative example, not a property: 24-sparse draws over a 352-wide block collide ~1.6 times in expectation. Over the 293 distinct real paths in the jail sample, off-diagonal code-block cosines have mean 0.0001 and max 0.25, and only 19.6% of pairs are exactly 0; my own one-trailing-character example gave 0.0435. The module DESCRIPTION says "near-orthogonal", which is accurate; the hypothesis's "0.0" is not.

divergences.claim: "the arch's file_read/file_write and path_read/path_write ... Those maps see a mean-pooled sentence embedding of the whole command" (lines 37-39).
divergences.what_the_code_does: file_read/file_write do take x_cmd = LayerNorm(cmd_proj(tok) + type + pos), so "linear map of the command token" is close enough. path_read/path_write take h_cmd0 = the post-transformer hidden state, which is not a linear map of the token. This is a description of the parent's mechanism, not of the new code, so it does not affect what gets scored.

divergences.claim: "All 724 commands in the jail sample parse under these rules: only cat, ls and mv appear, every argument is an absolute path" (lines 30-32).
divergences.what_the_code_does: 724 commands and the cat/ls/mv verb set are exactly right. 22 of them (bare `ls`, `ls -a`, `ls -ld`, `ls -ln`) carry no argument at all, so _parse returns src=dst="" and the code degenerates to verb block plus flags (14 nonzero coords instead of ~63). Handled gracefully — flags[0] correctly reports "no source" — but the "every argument is an absolute path" gloss glosses over argument-less commands.
